common_name: Afrotropical Highland Forest Fly (Multi-Spined Clasper Surstylus)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila teissieri (1.7 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.predecessor_atlas_note: Slot 2811 cell-tier pigment stripe (97.6 µm), not a detail-scale parameter copied into this model.
paleobiology.successor_atlas_note: D. virilis multi-scale atlas minimum (2.72 µm). Extant, subgenus Drosophila; not an anagenetic descendant of teissieri.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: du/dt = Du lap u + gamma (a - u + u^2 v); dv/dt = Dv lap v + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (Dv f_u + Du g_v) / (2 Du Dv)
equations.source: Turing 1952 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37, dispersion of a two-morphogen system; Schnakenberg 1979 JTB 81:389 for the reaction terms

parameters.note: Du is solved from the critical-wavenumber formula so lambda_c is 1.72 µm. These coefficients are not the slot-2761 power law (alpha=1.705, beta=0.316).

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 critical-wavenumber formula and the requirement that diffusion-driven instability needs unequal diffusivities and a stable homogeneous Jacobian.
Schnakenberg 1979 two-species reaction terms a - u + u^2 v and b - u^2 v.

Tsacas 1971 named Drosophila teissieri; GBIF 5074619 confirms the name. Tamura 2003/2004 dates the melanogaster-subgroup radiation with a mutation clock (lineage window 0–12 Ma used by this campaign).
reconstructed_in_script: Slot-specific (a, b, gamma, Dv/Du) = (0.13, 0.91, 1.15, 17.4) chosen so trace(J)<0, det(J)>0, and the formula wavelength is 1.72 µm on a 20.64 µm periodic patch.
Explicit-Euler integration, discrete-Laplacian dispersion check, and the magnified inset rendered on the vendored micrograph.
transfer_boundary: The 1.72 µm target is the campaign detail-scale assignment for this anatomical label, not a published measurement of teissieri pigment-granule spacing.
Predecessor 97.6 µm and successor 2.72 µm are atlas entries at other tiers, used only as chronoseries contrasts.
does_not_claim: That a named wet-lab paper measured a 1.72 µm Turing wavelength on D. teissieri.
That D. virilis is a descendant of D. teissieri, or that the gallery micrograph is a calibrated SEM of ocellar pigment.
That DOI 10.1093/molbev/msx210 is a teissieri Turing paper (Crossref: yeast de-novo genes).

specimen.license_note: Vendored gallery fallback. Wikimedia Commons had no CC bitmap for Drosophila teissieri on 2026-10-27.
specimen.scale_bar: 100 µm labeled; measured white bar is 111 px (0.901 µm/px).
